title: AWS SOA-C02 vs SAA-C03: SysOps or Architect?
subtitle: Day-to-day cloud ops or architecture design: which AWS Associate to target in 2026

pros: By far the most in-demand AWS cert — roughly 3x more job postings than the SOA (LinkedIn / WTTJ France, 2026).
Senior median salary of €65k in France, €70k in Luxembourg (Hays/APEC 2026) — the best cash ROI in the Associate lineup.
100% scenario-based multiple choice — no graded labs, so less technical stress on exam day.
The natural prerequisite for the SAP-C02 (Pro Architect) — about 70% of the content overlaps.
cons: A very wide surface (compute, storage, networking, security, cost, DR) — ~150 hours to truly master it.
Lots of 'pick the least-bad architecture' questions — tiring, subjective interpretation.
Very little real ops: no deep CloudWatch, no troubleshooting, no scripting.
On the job, you'll still be asked how to configure a VPC or an ASG — the SAA stays theoretical.
certs.bestFor: You're targeting Cloud Engineer, Architect, Consulting, Pre-sales or Platform Engineer — a role where you design more than you operate day to day.

pros: The only AWS Associate with graded labs (Exam Labs) — 3 hands-on scenarios in the Console: the closest match to real ops work.
Goes deep on operations: CloudWatch (logs/metrics/alarms), Systems Manager, Auto Scaling, backups, patching, Cost Explorer.
Recognized by Cloud Ops, FinOps, SRE teams and AWS MSPs — the cert that proves you can run the platform.
Slightly shorter prep (~130 hours) — less surface than the SAA, but more depth on Monitoring/Reporting.
cons: Employer recognition about 3x narrower than the SAA — many recruiters confuse it with the SAA and don't value it separately.
The graded labs are a trap: you need real-Console practice, and an interface glitch can cost you points.
Median salary comparable to a Cloud Ops engineer without the cert (~€55-60k senior in France) — the SOA alone doesn't push salary up.
Not the natural path to the SAP-C02 — the logical next step is the DOP-C02 (DevOps Pro).
certs.bestFor: You're a Cloud Ops engineer, SRE, or sysadmin moving to AWS day to day (CloudWatch, IAM, ASG, backups) and want to formalize what you already do.

verdicts.profile: You're undecided and want to maximize your interview chances.
verdicts.why: The SAA-C03 shows up in 3x more postings and virtually every cloud recruiter recognizes it — it is the default choice when your target role isn't locked in.

verdicts.profile: You're a sysadmin / Cloud Ops / SRE already operating AWS every day.
verdicts.why: The SOA-C02 validates exactly your job (CloudWatch, SSM, backups, patching). Its graded labs make it the only AWS Associate that tests what you actually do.

verdicts.profile: You're targeting Cloud Architect, AWS Consultant or Pre-sales.
verdicts.why: These roles expect the SAA as a prerequisite: its content (Well-Architected, multi-AZ, cost, DR, migration patterns) is exactly what gets tested in architecture interviews.

verdicts.profile: You want the best starting salary without a fixed target role.
verdicts.why: Senior median of ~€65k in France for the SAA vs ~€55-60k for an AWS Ops profile — the gap comes from the SAA opening better-paid consulting/architect roles.

verdicts.profile: You're ultimately aiming for the SAP-C02 (Solutions Architect Professional).
verdicts.why: The SAA-C03 is the natural prerequisite: about 70% of its content reappears in more depth on the SAP. The SOA would point you toward the DOP-C02 (DevOps Pro) instead.

verdicts.profile: You work at an AWS MSP or on a FinOps / 24/7 NOC team.
verdicts.why: The SOA is exactly the cert MSPs ask of their Ops engineers: CloudWatch, Systems Manager, Cost Explorer, automation — their daily work.

verdicts.profile: You're preparing an AWS partnership or bid for your company.
verdicts.why: AWS partner tiers (Select, Advanced, Premier) count SAA holders first. The SOA counts too, but with a lower weighting.

verdicts.profile: Graded labs make you panic / you're not comfortable in the AWS Console.
verdicts.why: The SAA is 100% multiple choice; the SOA has 3 graded labs where you click through the real Console under pressure. If hands-on testing stresses you, pick the SAA.

verdicts.profile: You want to pass both within 6 months.
verdicts.why: Start with the SAA-C03: it gives you the architectural context and half the services. You then follow with the SOA in ~70 extra hours instead of 130 from scratch.

tldr: SAA if you don't know which role to target, you're aiming for architect/consulting, or you want to avoid graded labs — it is the default AWS cert, better paid and more widely recognized. SOA only if you're a day-to-day Cloud Ops / SRE / AWS admin and want to formalize the Monitoring + Systems Manager work you already do.
